answer: Per-identity delta throttling caps each agent's net resource draw at a sliding-window delta; clones inherit their parent's consumption history, so a fresh copy starts already at the cap. Every identity also posts an ivory work-ledger audited by random zephyr probes, and a clone that fails to reproduce its parent's logged output forfeits the ledger balance. The marginal clone therefore costs a full audit bond plus lost throughput while earning zero, making duplication strictly negative-EV.
